column1: # The forwarder's vectors (the proxy record's forwarder, F-PLAN, section 9; read by core/net/src/forward/tests.rs and
# by the proxy lab's check.py). Written by hand from RFC 9112 and the clients' documented forms, never captured.
# Columns, tab-separated: the way (forward: the bytes to the proxy are the app's, each request line in absolute form
# and each Transfer-Encoding value written chunked; connect: a first head not forwarded, or a first request whose
# trailer came with its head, by CONNECT where one may still be tried, else a reset; reset: a later head or a body's
# framing refused, or a trailer read after its head went, the connection reset after what came before), why (the
# reason, as forward::Why names it, or -), the destination the app connected to, the names Datapavan's own resolvers
# gave it (comma-separated, lower case), the app's bytes, and the bytes to the proxy. Bytes escape \r, \n, \t, \\
# The last two columns are the proxy lab's, measured (scripts/proxylab/check.py; PROXYLAB_WRITE_VECTORS=PATH writes
# them anew): what the lab's target got from squid 6.13 and from tinyproxy 1.11.2 for a forward row the lab can carry,
# each request's line and Host (`LINE => HOST`, requests joined by ` ;; `, the proxy's own answer as `CODE from the
# proxy`), or - for a row the lab cannot carry. The proxy, not the engine, makes the origin's Host (the audit's m4).
